claims.claim: Slavova's sound-symbolic experiment selected twenty roughly one-page passages, drawn from works by seven authors including Robin Hobb.
claims.source: Velina Slavova, 'Towards Emotion Recognition in Texts - A Sound-Symbolic Experiment', International Journal of Cognitive Research in Science, Engineering and Education 7.2 (2019) 41-51
claims.quote: Twenty approximately one-page-long passages of text

claims.claim: Elliott's annotation reports that Shropshire's geography thesis codes Hobb's landscape passages as performing five functions, among them establishing verisimilitude, criticising social systems and denoting privilege and relative power.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, annotating Catherine Ann Shropshire, 'The Importance of Geographic Realism in Genre Fiction' (MS thesis, Oklahoma State University, 2019), in The Fedwren Project: A Robin Hobb Annotated Bibliography (last updated 18 May 2026)
claims.quote: establishing verisimilitude, criticizing social systems, denoting privilege and relative power

claims.claim: Elliott's annotation reports that Crane and Fletcher read the Liveship Traders novels as inverting the usual depiction of land as busy and sea as empty.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, annotating Ralph Crane and Lisa Fletcher, 'An Imaginary Water World: Robin Hobb's The Liveship Traders Trilogy' (2017), in The Fedwren Project
claims.quote: inverting the usual depiction of land as busy and sea
claims.page: entry: Crane, Ralph, and Lisa Fletcher

claims.claim: Elliott's annotation records that Mendlesohn's taxonomy places Hobb's Elderlings corpus as an example of portal-quest fantasy.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, annotating Farah Mendlesohn, Rhetorics of Fantasy (2008), in The Fedwren Project
claims.quote: offering an example of the portal-quest fantasy in the Elderlings corpus

claims.claim: Tkach and Volkova find Hobb's Six Duchies naming built on a principle of national-cultural contrast.
claims.source: Polina Tkach (National Academy of the National Guard of Ukraine) and Maryna Volkova (Kharkiv National Air Force University), "Robin Hobb's 'The World of the Elderlings' Onomasticon: The Structural and Functional Significance of Charactonyms", Perspectives and Innovations of Science 5(47) (2026) 372-381
claims.quote: meticulously constructed upon the fundamental principle of national-cultural contrast

claims.claim: They report that names for the neighbouring nations - Eyod, Rurisk, Kettricken - are phonetically foreign and carry no transparent semantics for the reader.
claims.source: Tkach and Volkova, Perspectives and Innovations of Science 5(47) (2026) 372-381
claims.quote: phonetic foreignness and an absolute lack of transparent semantics

claims.claim: Socially significant anthroponyms are the largest group in Hobb's naming, which the authors read as mirroring a setting where social mask, status and destiny are bound together.
claims.source: Tkach and Volkova, Perspectives and Innovations of Science 5(47) (2026) 372-381
claims.quote: a person's social mask, status, and destiny are inextricably linked

claims.claim: Names such as Shrewd, Desire and Patience are treated as direct psychological characterisation carried by the name itself.
claims.source: Tkach and Volkova, Perspectives and Innovations of Science 5(47) (2026) 372-381

claims.claim: Srsic notes that the Liveship Traders characters call the woman known only as Mother by that role and never by a name, and that her name is never given.
claims.source: Petra Srsic (University of Osijek), 'Motherhood, Disability, and Rebellion: Constructing the Mother in Hobb's Liveship Traders Trilogy', Studia Anglica Resoviensia 22 (2025) 145-157
claims.quote: they always refer to her as Mother, never by her name

claims.claim: Elliott reads Hobb's novella Words like Coins as a commentary on the craft of writing that warns against sloppiness of language.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'Sample Conference-length Paper: Searching the Hoard in Words like Coins', Geoffrey B. Elliott's Teaching Blog, 29 July 2013
claims.quote: serves as a commentary on the craft of writing

claims.claim: In Elliott's reading the pecksies of that novella repeatedly press for linguistic precision and frugality.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'Searching the Hoard in Words like Coins' (2013)
claims.quote: Linguistic precision and frugality are repeatedly emphasized by the pecksie

claims.claim: Elliott says the pecksies keep their own utterances exact, giving no more than is needed to be clear, so as to limit unintended consequences.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'Searching the Hoard in Words like Coins' (2013)
claims.quote: giving no more than is necessary to be clear

claims.claim: Elliott traces the novella's central disaster - a near-fatal childbirth - to the protagonist's imprecise wording of a charm.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'Searching the Hoard in Words like Coins' (2013)
claims.quote: all as a result of Mirrifen's lack of specificity

claims.claim: Borowska-Szerszun, relayed by Wikipedia, contrasts Martin's focus on the brutality of realism with Hobb's focus on the psychological aspects of trauma.
claims.source: Wikipedia, 'Liveship Traders', Style section, relaying Sylwia Borowska-Szerszun, Extrapolation 60.1 (2019) 1-22
claims.quote: Hobb's narrative focuses more on the psychological aspects of trauma

claims.claim: Borowska-Szerszun's own abstract says Hobb's novels reframe the traditional rape script by shifting emphasis to the survivor.
claims.source: Sylwia Borowska-Szerszun, 'Representation of Rape in George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire and Robin Hobb's Liveship Traders', Extrapolation 60.1 (2019) 1-22 - abstract only, via the OpenAlex record
